scheduling.skillGoal: Review prose for comprehension-impeding communication issues and emit minimal-fix suggestions in a three-column markdown table, preserving content and author voice
scheduling.intentSignature: Clinical copy-edit prose for communication issues, output a three-column fix table
intentSignatures: Clinical copy-edit prose for communication issues, output a three-column fix table
Review prose for clarity and comprehension issues
Improve the prose with minimal-intervention fixes
Run an editorial review on a passage of text
triggerPatterns: user asks to improve the prose

ioContract.inputsRaw: content (required) — Cohesive unit of text to review (markdown, plain text, or text-heavy XML). style_guide (optional) — Project-specific style guide overriding all generic principles except CONTENT IS SACROSANCT. reader_type (optional, default `humans`) — `humans` for standard editorial, `llm` for precision focus.
ioContract.outputsRaw: Three-column markdown table with columns Original Text | Revised Text | Changes; otherwise the literal string 'No editorial issues identified'. HALT errors when content is empty/<3 words or reader_type is invalid.

preconditions: reader_type is `humans` or `llm` (or omitted, defaulting to `humans`)
code blocks, frontmatter, and structural markup are detectable so they can be skipped

structural.sceneGoal: Validate inputs, identify content type, and note skip-zones (code blocks, frontmatter, markup)
Analyze style, tone, and voice; calibrate review priorities by reader_type
Review prose, identify issues, determine minimal fixes, and merge/dedup overlapping entries
Output the three-column fix table when issues are found; otherwise output 'No editorial issues identified'

logical.description: If content is empty or contains fewer than 3 words, HALT with the documented error message
If reader_type is not `humans` or `llm` (and is provided), HALT with the documented error message
Identify content type (markdown, plain text, XML with text) and note any code blocks, frontmatter, or structural markup to skip
Analyze the style, tone, and voice of the input text; note intentional stylistic choices to preserve

Calibrate review priorities by reader_type — `llm` favors unambiguous references, consistent terminology, explicit structure, no hedging; `humans` favors clarity, flow, readability, natural progression
If style_guide was provided, consult it now and treat its requirements as overriding all generic principles for this review (except CONTENT IS SACROSANCT)
Walk all prose sections (skipping code blocks, frontmatter, structural markup) to identify communication issues that impede comprehension
For each issue, determine the minimal fix that achieves clarity and phrase uncertain fixes as 'Consider: [suggestion]?' queries
Deduplicate same-issue occurrences into one entry listing all locations, merge overlapping issues into single entries, and preserve author voice
If issues found, output the three-column markdown table (Original Text | Revised Text | Changes); otherwise output the literal 'No editorial issues identified'
